arxiv-2003-09975.title: The Distributive Full Lambek Calculus with Modal Operators
arxiv-2003-09975.creator: Daniel Rogozin
arxiv-2003-09975.description: Abstract In this paper, we study logics of bounded distributive residuated lattices with modal operators considering □ \Box and ◇ \Diamond in a noncommutative setting. We introduce relational semantics for such substructural modal logics. We prove that any canonical logic is Kripke complete via discrete duality and canonical extensions.

arxiv-2107-14785.title: Rooted Clusters for Graph LP Algebras
arxiv-2107-14785.creator: Esther BANAIAN a, Sunita CHEPURI b, Elizabeth KELLEY c and Sylvester W. ZHANG d
arxiv-2107-14785.description: Abstract LP algebras, introduced by Lam and Pylyavskyy, are a generalization of cluster algebras. These algebras are known to have the Laurent phenomenon, but positivity remains conjectural. Graph LP algebras are finite LP algebras encoded by a graph. For the graph LP algebra defined by a tree, we define a family of clusters called rooted clusters .

arxiv-2110-05905.title: Nucleosome sliding can influence the spreading of histone modifications
arxiv-2110-05905.creator: Shantanu Kadam 1* , Tripti Bameta 2* , Ranjith Padinhateeri
arxiv-2110-05905.description: Abstract Nucleosomes are the fundamental building blocks of chromatin that not only help in the folding of chromatin but also in carrying epigenetic information. It is known that nucleosome sliding is responsible for dynamically organizing chromatin structure and the resulting gene regulation.

arxiv-2202-09617.title: Search for Higgs boson pair production in the four \PQb quark final state in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2202-09617.description: Abstract A search for pairs of Higgs bosons produced via gluon and vector boson fusion is presented, focusing on the four \PQb quark final state. The data sample consists of proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV , collected with the CMS detector at the LHC, and corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 138 \fbinv .

arxiv-2209-10025.title: Small atoms fall into bulk from non-close-packed surfaces?
arxiv-2209-10025.creator: Shota Ono, Honoka Satomi, Junji Yuhara
arxiv-2209-10025.description: Abstract Surface rippling has been observed when atoms of X X and A A are mixed on the A A substrate surface. The rippling amplitude has been estimated using hard sphere models. We present a gedanken experiment predicting a penetration of small atoms into bulk through the (100) surface.

arxiv-2307-12194.title: LIST: Learning Implicitly from Spatial Transformers for Single-View 3D Reconstruction
arxiv-2307-12194.creator: Mohammad Samiul Arshad, William J. Beksi
arxiv-2307-12194.description: Abstract Accurate reconstruction of both the geometric and topological details of a 3D object from a single 2D image embodies a fundamental challenge in computer vision. Existing explicit/implicit solutions to this problem struggle to recover self-occluded geometry and/or faithfully reconstruct topological shape structures.

arxiv-2311-06730.title: Stability analysis for large-scale multi-agent molecular communication systems
arxiv-2311-06730.creator: Taishi Kotsuka, Yutaka Hori
arxiv-2311-06730.description: Abstract Molecular communication (MC) is recently featured as a novel communication tool to connect individual biological nanorobots. It is expected that a large number of nanorobots can form large multi-agent MC systems through MC to accomplish complex and large-scale tasks that cannot be achieved by a single nanorobot.

arxiv-2409-04372.title: Kohn–Sham inversion with mathematical guarantees
arxiv-2409-04372.creator: Michael F. Herbst, Vebjørn H. Bakkestuen, Andre Laestadius
arxiv-2409-04372.description: Abstract We use an exact Moreau-Yosida regularized formulation to obtain the exchange-correlation potential for periodic systems. We reveal a profound connection between rigorous mathematical principles and efficient numerical implementation, which marks the first computation of a Moreau–Yosida-based inversion for physical systems.

arxiv-2501-04544.title: Ray transform of symmetric tensor fields on Riemannian manifolds with conjugate points
arxiv-2501-04544.creator: Sean Holman ∗ and Venkateswaran P. Krishnan †
arxiv-2501-04544.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sean Holman ∗ and Venkateswaran P. Krishnan †. In this article, we study the microlocal properties of the geodesic ray transform of symmetric m m -tensor fields on 2-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with boundary allowing the possibility of conjugate points.

arxiv-2501-12833.title: A coupled FE-BE multi-scale method for the dynamics of jointed structures
arxiv-2501-12833.creator: Hendrik D. Linder 1 , Johann Groß 1 , Malte Krack 1 ,
arxiv-2501-12833.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hendrik D. Linder 1 , Johann Groß 1 , Malte Krack 1 ,. The damping of built-up structures stems largely from the microscopic dry frictional interactions in the contact interfaces. The accurate prediction of friction damping has been an important scientific aim of the past several decades.

arxiv-2503-13784.title: SwarmUpdate: Hierarchical Software Updates and Deep Learning Model Patching for Heterogeneous UAV Swarms
arxiv-2503-13784.creator: Lin Geng, Hao Li, Sidney Givigi, Bram Adams
arxiv-2503-13784.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lin Geng, Hao Li, Sidney Givigi, Bram Adams. Heterogeneous unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms consist of dozens to hundreds of drones with different roles and varying hardware and software requirements collaborating towards a shared mission.

arxiv-2504-02639.title: Reservoir Computing: A New Paradigm for Neural Networks
arxiv-2504-02639.creator: Felix Grezes
arxiv-2504-02639.description: Abstract \makeabstractpage Pr. Andrew Rosenberg Introduction: Even before Artificial Intelligence was its own field of computational science, humanity has tried to mimic the activity of the human brain. In the early 1940s the first artificial neuron models were created as purely mathematical concepts. Over the years, ideas from neuroscience and computer science were used to develop the modern Neural Network.

arxiv-2507-11474.title: HUG-VAS: A Hierarchical NURBS-Based Generative Model for Aortic Geometry Synthesis and Controllable Editing Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2507-11474.creator: Pan Du, Mingqi Xu, Xiaozhi Zhu, Jian-xun Wang
arxiv-2507-11474.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pan Du, Mingqi Xu, Xiaozhi Zhu, Jian-xun Wang. Accurate characterization of vascular geometry is essential for cardiovascular diagnosis and treatment planning. Traditional statistical shape modeling (SSM) methods rely on linear assumptions, limiting their expressivity and scalability to complex topologies such as multi-branch vascular structures. We introduce HUG-VAS, a Hierarchical NURBS Generative model for Vascular geometry Synthesis, which integrates NURBS surface parameterization with diffusion-based generative modeling to synthesize realistic, fine-grained aortic geometries.

arxiv-2509-11083.title: An Alignment-Free Explanation for Collective Predator Evasion in Moving Animal Groups
arxiv-2509-11083.creator: Daniel Strömbom, Catherine Futterman
arxiv-2509-11083.description: Abstract Moving animal groups consist of many distinct individuals but can operate and function as one unit when performing different tasks. Effectively evading unexpected predator attacks is one primary task for many moving groups. The current explanation for predator evasion responses in moving animal groups require the individuals in the groups interact via (velocity) alignment.

pmc-10627167.title: Impact of Prone Jackknife Position on Intraoperative Hypotension During Percutaneous Nephroscopy: A Retrospective Matched Analysis
pmc-10627167.creator: Song Lyu, Guobin Wu, Yingfen Wu
pmc-10627167.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the potential relationship between the prone jackknife position during percutaneous nephroscopy and the occurrence of intraoperative hypotension.MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted on 651 patients who underwent percutaneous nephroscopy at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Hainan Medical University. The primary focus was to investigate the occurrence of hypotension during the surgical procedure and assess the duration of hypotensive episodes.

pmc-10672608.title: Constraints on Optimising Encoder-Only Transformers for Modelling Sign Language with Human Pose Estimation Keypoint Data
pmc-10672608.creator: Luke T Woods, Zeeshan A Rana, Antonio Fernández-Caballero
pmc-10672608.description: Supervised deep learning models can be optimised by applying regularisation techniques to reduce overfitting, which can prove difficult when fine tuning the associated hyperparameters. Not all hyperparameters are equal, and understanding the effect each hyperparameter and regularisation technique has on the performance of a given model is of paramount importance in research.

pmc-10679821.title: Distribution characteristics and potential risks of bioaerosols during scattered farming
pmc-10679821.creator: Xuezheng Yu, Yunping Han, Jianguo Liu, Yingnan Cao, Ying Wang, Zixuan Wang, Jinxin Lyu, Ziyu Zhou, Ying Yan, Yuxiang Zhang
pmc-10679821.description: SummaryIn most economically underdeveloped areas, scattered farming and human‒livestock cohabitation are common. However, production of bioaerosols and their potential harm in these areas have not been previously researched. In this study, bioaerosol characteristics were analyzed in scattered farming areas in rural Northwest China.

pmc-11356781.title: HIV Care in Ukrainian Migrants in Two European Countries: All the Same?
pmc-11356781.creator: Kathrin van Bremen, Miłosz Parczewski, Malte Monin, Magdalena Leszczyszyn-Pynka, Stefan Schlabe, Franciszek Lenkiewicz, Malwina Karasińska-Cieślak, Jan-Christian Wasmuth, Magdalena Witak-Jędra, Sven Breitschwerdt, Jürgen K Rockstroh, Dmytro Zhyvytsia, Christoph Boesecke, Daniel Chober, Bogusz Aksak-
pmc-11356781.description: Introduction: War in Ukraine prompted an enormous refugee influx into Europe, including approximately 4200 people with HIV. The unique healthcare features of Ukrainian refugees living with HIV were compared between two infectious disease departments in Bonn, Germany, and Szczecin, Poland.

pmc-12626939.title: Mechanisms of aging in the cardiovascular system: challenges and opportunities
pmc-12626939.creator: Xiaoying Zhao, Xinyue Yang, Yumeng Lin, Ruolan Lei, Wei Ding, Xinying He, Ying Cao, Dechou Zhang, Ping Liu, Meirou Liang, Zhongyu Han, Yu Jiang
pmc-12626939.description: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) pose a significant threat to the health of the elderly population. As the global population ages and medical management remains imperfect, reducing the medical burden of CVDs is of great importance. Aging is a complex process that contributes to the development and progression of CVDs through various mechanisms.

pmc-12683332.title: Thinking about returning home from a protected haematology unit: confronting healthcare providers’ representations and patients’ experiences in a qualitative study
pmc-12683332.creator: Sandrine Letrecher, Yasmine Chemrouk, Livia Sani
pmc-12683332.description: BackgroundThe psychological impact of protective isolation in haematology has been widely studied during hospitalization, but little is known about what happens when patients return home.AimDrawing on two qualitative studies conducted in French hospitals—one with patients and one with healthcare providers—this article explores how both groups experience the transition out of protective isolation.

pmc-13386584.title: Day-to-day variability in resting metabolic rate in strength athletes
pmc-13386584.creator: Claire Buechel, Kate Pumpa, Naroa Etxebarria, Luke Ashton, Michelle Minehan
pmc-13386584.description: BackgroundResting Metabolic Rate (RMR) is measured in sport settings for health monitoring and nutrition planning; however, interpreting repeated measures requires an understanding of typical day-to-day variability under habitual, free-living conditions. This study quantified intra-individual variability in RMR among weight-stable strength-trained athletes, examined the impact of data processing approaches, and established protocol-specific least significant change (LSC) thresholds under ecological conditions.

uslaw-usc-t5-s3341.title: 5 U.S.C. § 3341 — Details; within Executive or military departments
uslaw-usc-t5-s3341.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t5-s3341.description: United States Code, Title 5 (Government Organization And Employees); Part III (Employees); Subpart B (Employment And Retention); Chapter 33 (Examination, Selection, And Placement); Subchapter III (Details, Vacancies, And Appointments). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The head of an Executive department or military department may detail employees among the bureaus and offices of his department, except employees who are required by law.
